stories.headline: Russian bombs kill 24 at a Ukrainian aid centre
body: A Russian bomb attack on a school used as an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhia, killed 24 people.
Zelenskyy said a second wave of nine bombs hit the shelter where people had gathered.
Five others were injured; he called it proof Russia doesn't want de-escalation.
stories.vc: Attacks like this dim hopes for the US-led peace talks that markets have been watching.

image.credit: National Police of Ukraine / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Hackers hit supermarket fridges across seven European countries
body: Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden saw fridge and freezer temperatures soar overnight.
Some reached 50°C, destroying food; Ikea was among the shops hit.
It echoes a cyber-attack on French shops last month that caused millions of euros in damage.
stories.joke: Your ice cream's biggest enemy is now a hacker.
stories.vc: Connected building systems are a growing cyber weak spot, pushing retailers to spend more on industrial security.

stories.headline: UN ends its 35-year Western Sahara peacekeeping mission
body: The UN mission in disputed Western Sahara stopped work on Sunday after 35 years.
It ended because of a US–Russia standoff at the UN over the territory's future.
Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front both claim the mineral-rich territory.
stories.vc: Instability in Western Sahara could affect phosphate and fishing deals that Morocco depends on.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 1,233 points; Nifty crosses 23,400
body: The Sensex rose 1,233 points on Monday, and the Nifty gained 388 points to 23,440.
It was the third straight day of gains, helped by a sharp rise in Reliance shares.
Brent crude fell 3% to about $110 a barrel on hopes for US–Iran talks, easing India's import worries.
stories.joke: The Sensex had a great Monday. Most of us just had Monday.
stories.vc: Strong rallies help the queue of upcoming IPOs and lift startup valuations tied to listed peers.

stories.headline: Global firms bid to design India's first 'AI township' near Bengaluru
body: Global companies have bid to design and plan the Bidadi township, billed as India's first AI-powered township.
Karnataka has now issued final land notifications for all nine villages needed.
Farmers opposing the project have protested for over 560 days.
stories.vc: A planned AI city could pull data centres and tech firms west of Bengaluru, if the land fight is resolved.

stories.headline: Policybazaar parent hits new low over insurance rule fears
body: PB Fintech shares fell about 8% to a 52-week low of ₹926, down 48% since 23 September.
That's when insurance regulator IRDAI proposed an overhaul of insurance rules.
Brokerages are split, with ratings from 'Reduce' to 'Outperform'.
stories.joke: Comparing insurance plans is easy. Comparing regulator drafts, less so.
stories.vc: Regulatory risk can wipe out half a company's value fast, a key lesson for fintech investors.

stories.headline: Marvell buys Lumentum in one of tech's biggest deals ever
body: Chip designer Marvell will buy optical chip maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal worth $115 billion including debt.
It's bigger than Microsoft's $68.7 billion Activision deal.
Both companies count Nvidia as a major shareholder.
stories.joke: Two chip firms, one Nvidia-shaped friend in common.
stories.vc: Optical links that move data between AI chips are the next bottleneck, and that's what Marvell is buying.

image.credit: The Conmunity -  Pop Culture Geek from Los Angeles, CA, USA / Wikimedia Commons

stories.statLabel: biggest US carrier it could become
stories.headline: SpaceX reportedly wants to buy Boost Mobile
body: SpaceX is looking to buy Boost Mobile from EchoStar, the Washington Post reports.
It would help build a mixed cellular–satellite network and could make SpaceX the fourth-biggest US carrier.
SpaceX already bought $17 billion of wireless spectrum from EchoStar last year.
stories.joke: Rockets, satellites, AI chips, and now your phone plan.
stories.vc: Satellite-plus-cellular could shake up telecom pricing everywhere, including India where Starlink is entering.

stories.statLabel: AI firms named in the suit
stories.headline: New York Times sues Brave over scraping its content for AI
body: The New York Times sued privacy browser Brave, saying it scraped its content and passed it to AI firms.
The suit names Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere as customers.
The Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel filed a similar suit.
stories.joke: The newspaper vs the browser. Plot twist: the AI is the reader.
stories.vc: Copyright suits could force AI firms to pay for news data, a new revenue stream for publishers.

stories.headline: Musk throttles Grok Bot because it costs too much to run
body: Grok Bot users found their weekly limits suddenly maxed out over the weekend.
Elon Musk said serving Grok Bot was 'unsustainably high' in cost relative to revenue.
Some users said their usage jumped from 50% to 100% overnight.
stories.joke: Even AI agents have a spending limit now. Relatable.
stories.vc: AI agents are expensive to run; pricing them profitably is the next big test for every AI company.

stories.headline: Squarespace lays off about 300 people
body: Website builder Squarespace is cutting about 19% of its workforce, roughly 300 jobs.
It says it wants to simplify and move faster.
Website building has changed a lot as AI tools spread.
stories.vc: AI site builders are squeezing older web platforms, forcing cost cuts across the sector.

image.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Bridgit Mendler's space startup hits a $2 billion valuation
body: Northwood Space raised $375 million led by a16z and DFJ Growth, valuing it at $2 billion.
It builds antennas and software that help satellites talk to Earth.
Its CEO and co-founder is former actress Bridgit Mendler; it also has a near-$50 million US Space Force contract.
stories.joke: From Disney Channel to deep space. Quite the career pivot.
stories.vc: Women still lead a small share of venture-backed hard-tech firms; big rounds like this help change the pattern.

stories.headline: Women who could make history in Tuesday's US elections
body: The 19th is tracking women who could break barriers in Tuesday's midterms.
Deb Haaland is favoured in New Mexico and would be the first Native woman to lead any US state.
Two other women are likely to become the first women governors of their states.
stories.joke: Firsts in 2026. Better late than never.
stories.vc: More women governors tend to prioritise childcare and healthcare budgets, shaping state spending.

stories.headline: State attorney general races could decide abortion access
body: Thirty US states are electing attorneys general, their top lawyers, this year.
Since Roe was overturned, they have defended or challenged abortion access, even across state lines.
Some are suing states with shield laws that protect doctors who mail abortion pills.
stories.vc: Legal fights over abortion pills shape the market for telehealth and reproductive-health startups.

stories.headline: Udupi's new district hospital nears its opening
body: The opening date for Udupi's new district hospital will be decided at a meeting with Karnataka's health minister in Bengaluru.
District minister Rizwan Arshad said he will inspect the hospital first.
Officials and elected representatives will join talks on its issues.
stories.vc: New district hospitals bring specialist care closer to home and cut costly trips to big cities.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu may turn Tambaram hospital into a medical college
body: Tamil Nadu is considering upgrading Tambaram District Government Hospital into a full medical college.
Health minister KG Arunraj will discuss it with the Chief Minister before announcing it.
The state also plans advance slot booking for medicines on its Nalam AI health platform.
stories.vc: Medical colleges add beds and doctors at once, the fastest way to grow public hospital capacity.

stories.headline: Kerala shortlists 10 sites for its long-awaited AIIMS
body: Kerala has shared about 10 possible sites for an AIIMS with the Union health minister.
It is studying feasibility reports from district authorities.
The state first proposed an AIIMS in 2014.
stories.joke: Twelve years of waiting. Ten options. One AIIMS.
stories.vc: An AIIMS anchors a whole health ecosystem of colleges, clinics and jobs around it.

stories.headline: Gujarat opens a new cancer hospital in Patan
body: Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel opened the PB Patan Janata Cancer Hospital, run by a charitable trust.
It has a ₹22 crore linear accelerator for radiotherapy.
It brings PET scans to North Gujarat for the first time, free for Ayushman Bharat cardholders.
stories.vc: Charity-run cancer centres fill big gaps outside metros, where private chains rarely build.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1's youngest world champion
body: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli clinched the title at 20 years and 68 days by finishing third in Mexico City.
He is Italy's first champion since 1953 and beats Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest.
Max Verstappen won the red-flagged race; Lewis Hamilton was second after clashing with teammate Leclerc.
stories.joke: Most 20-year-olds celebrate passing exams. He won the world.
stories.vc: A young, charismatic champion is gold for F1's sponsors, TV deals and Mercedes' brand value.
